ex: Can I just say anyone who's offended by this, he means no harm. He doesn't. He knows not what he says, really everything from Karl is totally genuine. He's not having a go. You Live and Let Live, don't you? There is a...
He's a bit, he's a bit like Mork from Mork and Mindy.
He hasn't got a prejudicial bone in his body, but go on then.

q: Karl wanted cockroach people as dustmen and ant people as builders. What did Steve point out they couldn't do?
f: Karl was having none of it: "No, but they wouldn't be doing that job. They're just doing the bins."
ex: Could they still sort out the rubbish if they've got no heads?
Except they. If they were, because you know, you want to use them as builders and dustmen. They couldn't whistle at pretty girls, could they?
No, but they wouldn't be doing that job. They're just doing the bins.

q: Why did Steve suspect donkeys were deliberately "picking us off one by one"?
a: They're annoyed at being called "ass" and made to wear little hats
x: They're jealous that horses get to race
Revenge for being left out of the Nativity
They're fed up of eating nothing but straw
f: Steve also blamed giving kids rides on the beach: "I don't think it's accident. I think they're pickin' us off."
ex: Well I think that's what's happening. I don't think it's accident. I think they're pickin' us off. I think--
They're so annoyed that a nickname for them is "ass"--
And they've got to wear the little hat, you know, they get- they've got to ride kid- you know, give kids rides on the beach and that. I think they're just, sort of, annoyed.
Maybe they're just, sort of, picking us off one by one.

q: Steve accidentally called stand-in presenter Claire Sturgess 'Karl'. After blaming the 'C' sound, what did he tell her?
a: Claire is quite an unmemorable name
x: She sits in Karl's chair, so it's her fault
Everyone at XFM gets called Karl eventually
Karl had asked him to say his name on air
f: Ricky had already asked: "Is it the shaved head or the stupidity?" Steve also thought he'd called her Arthur or Jack the last time she filled in.
ex: Well, I don't know if you've heard this, Karl. Uh, Karl? I've called you Karl.
That's okay. I'm Claire, pleased to meet you.
Is it the shaved head or the stupidity?
It was the 'C' sound. Because didn't I call you Arthur or Jack or something last time?

q: As he leapt off the roof onto crash mats for his stunt, what was Steve petrified might get broken?
f: It's the same reason he's never had a fight: "I could never get into fights or go in a mosh pit because of my glasses."
ex: Well, we were up on a roof, and obviously they had the crash mats and stuff and I had to kind of leap off… uhm and land on the mats and stuff. And obviously I was petrified the whole time ‘cause I was wearing my glasses…

…petrified that they might get broken. So I was, like, not really doing it properly and kind of leaping like, like, you know people when they can’t dive into a swimming pool so they put that one foot out first to sort of…
Was it you, was it you that told me that you could, you could never get into fights…
No, I could never get into fights or go in a mosh pit because of my glasses.

q: Told St Patrick rid Ireland of snakes, Karl asked who'd done the job in England, as there aren't many here. What was Steve's explanation?
a: St Patrick had a go here too, but got tired and went back
x: St George did it once he ran out of dragons
The RSPCA moved them all to zoos
Henry VIII had them all banned
f: Steve: "I think he had a stab at it over here as well, but got tired, went back. That's why there's a few snakes here."
ex: And there are no snakes in Ireland.
He rid Ireland of all the snakes.
Who did it ‘ere then, ‘cause there aren’t that many.
Well, I think he had a stab at it over here as well, but got tired, went back.
That’s why there’s a few snakes here. Is it true that there are no snakes in Ireland.

q: Karl protested that he was already treating Suzanne to the pictures. How did Steve imagine Karl got in on the cheap?
a: Dressed as a small child: "Me and my son, please!"
x: Claimed he was a film critic
f: Tickets were eight quid each. Ricky's version: Karl made Suzanne sit on his shoulders and wear a long coat.
ex: (laughing) How much was that? That was eight quid each. Did you pay for it though?
If I know you, you had a dressed up as a small child.
Or you made her sit on your shoulder as wear a long coat.

q: Discussing whether Nelson said "Kiss me, Hardy" or "Kismet", what did Steve reckon Nelson's actual dying breath was?
f: Ricky had heard both "Kismet", which also means fate, and "kiss me, kiss me". Steve's version: "I think his final actual dying breath was 'no tongues.'"
ex: Well, I don't know. I don't know about this because I heard that he didn't and it said Kismet, which also means fate. And then I heard that he did say kiss me, kiss me.
Hardy. Like, you know, because it, well it creates suspense. I don't know. Is it, is it Kismet or is it kiss me?
Kiss me Hardy. I think his final actual dying breath was 'no tongues.'

q: Steve said he'd been hit by global warming. How long did his plane to the States sit on the runway being de-iced?
f: Steve wanted them to warm it up like his car: "pop inside for another cup of tea, come back out, it's lovely and warm and toasty in there."
s: The Ricky Gervais Guide to The Earth · 2010
ex: I've been hit by global warming recently, Rick. A couple of times, actually. I don't want to be one of those people that's like "Oh, you know, because of the snow and the rain... that's obviously do with global warming" but it probably is.…

And on the old plane... One of those bleak, kind of snowy days recently. They got us all on the plane. We sat on the runway. For four and a half hours! Four and a half hours, while they de-iced the plane. Now, it's good that they de-iced…
Okay? Let it warm up, pop inside for another cup of tea, come back out, it's lovely and warm and toasty in there. That's what I'd like to see them do with the old plane.

q: In the revived "Make Ricky Gervais Laugh" game, Steve said the bespectacled, stubbly rock star in the Sun photo looked like which puppet?
f: Steve: "He looks like he is a muppet... made of foam." He then declared the game's comeback "a roaring success."
ex: I'll tell you who he looks like, he looks like Zig I think from Zig and Zag.
He looks like he is a muppet….
Nice to see that game come back.

q: Steve landed a part in a BBC comedy pilot. What was his six-foot-seven character trying to win?
f: A rival "beats me every year 'cause he's slightly taller," but this year Steve's been training. Ricky: "That's the conflict."
ex: It’s a, it’s a, I play a very tall guy, like a sort of...
That’s the part ah, that’s the part though isn’t it? About you got a beard?
I’m a character who’s, ah six foot seven inches tall and I’m trying to win the world’s, ah, tallest man competition.
That’s it, that’s it, yeah, yeah.
But, ah, there’s always a man that beats me every year ‘cause he’s slightly taller, but this year I think for some reason, because I’ve been training that I can beat ‘im.

q: Steve wanted a workout video hosted by Elle Macpherson or Cindy Crawford. Whose did his housemate buy?
f: His mate's excuse: "It was the cheapest one, Steve." Steve: "Thanks very much, mate."
ex: …a sort of hour-long workout. And I said to him, get one of the ones that’s hosted by like uhm…

…Elle Macpherson or Cindy Crawford, you know, you know, someone like that, someone sexy, right? So I swear to God, we went down this morning, we put it on, right? Just want you to picture this scene, right? It’s me, and my mate, in our…
…right? That was—“It was the cheapest one, Steve,” he told me. Thanks very much, mate.

q: The woman who wrote the list emailed in. Why did she say Steve wasn't that unlikely a lust object after all?
x: Tall men are back in fashion
He has a lovely radio voice
f: She also offered Steve her phone number. Ricky's take: "A sense of humour's important. That's a downer, innit?"
ex: "I wouldn't waste my time, the flaming cheek. Although it's a horrible picture I am of course in real life a vision of loveliness. I am not thirty-eight, I'm twenty-five. I don't think Steven's that unlikely lust object. A sense of…
A sense of humour's important. That's a downer, innit?

q: How did Steve hypothetically plan to get onto a nudist beach without stripping at the door?
a: Swim up to it in a wetsuit
x: Dig a tunnel under the dunes
Hide in an ice cream van
f: Steve's "fairly good swimmer" had time on his hands for a week. Ricky's twist: he was swimming there "From France!"
ex: Would it be possible for a bloke who was, say, a fairly good swimmer to swim up to the beach in a wetsuit--
Just say, just say for the sake of it that this person, you know, had some time on his hands for a week.

q: Ricky pointed out that Karl didn't have the facts either, and "he runs the radio station!" How did Steve correct him?
a: They just keep him there like a mascot
x: He's actually still on work experience
He's only there to water the plants
f: Steve said: "He's like a pet, isn't he? They have him runnin' around the office."
ex: He hasn't got the facts and he runs the radio station!
He doesn't run it, they keep him here like a mascot! He's like a pet, isn't he? They have him runnin' around the office.

q: According to Ricky, what did Steve once do to their mate Johnny's Doctor Who magazine?
a: Stuck post-it notes saying 'Geek' on every page
x: Drew moustaches on all the Daleks
Swapped its pages with the TV Times
f: Johnny opened it on the tube. Ricky then claimed the latest issue's drawing of the perfect Doctor Who fan "looks exactly like Steve."
ex: Karl, you know our mate Johnny? He's a "Doctor Who" fan.

Do you remember, um, he bought, um, uh, the "Doctor Who" magazine, um, and, uhh, he went, um, to the toilet and Steve got post-it notes and put "Geek" on every page. And Johnny opened it on the tube, right, and it had "geek" and…
All right. Don't have a go, Rick.

It does. He won't- and I- I- it- I- I'm gonna try and put it on the website. It's amazing! It's got your hair, glasses, it stands like you, it's, sort of, dressed like you and it's only carrying- (Laughs) it's hilarious and he's- he's-…

q: Steve read about a man who died falling out of a window while mooning. What did he say would have been a better last gag to die after?
a: A two-hour impromptu Eddie Izzard-style routine
x: A whoopee cushion at a wedding
f: Ricky: "Mooning isn't funny enough." Steve: "It's just not a good enough gag." He called the death "almost karmic".
ex: No. It's just not a good enough gag.
Do you know what I mean? It's a witless sort of thing to do and then to be killed for it.
If you just done a two hour impromptu Eddie Izard-style routine and then you got tragically killed, that would sort of make sense.
But mooning, it's almost karmic because it's such a bad joke.

q: Aged 11 or 12, Steve and a friend hosted their own radio show from a bedroom. With no transmitter, how did they broadcast it?
a: Through speakers hidden in the bushes of the front garden
x: By shouting through the neighbours' letterboxes
Over the school tannoy at lunchtime
By posting cassette tapes round the street
f: Steve hoped girls would stop and listen: "These guys are great. I dunno where these sounds are coming from, it seems to be that bush..."
ex: Do you know what it reminds me of? When I was young, I wanted to get into radio, I was excited about radio, and I was sort of in my - I dunno, I was 11 or 12. My friend and I, we got a little mixing deck, and we used to host our own radio…
Uh, from his bedroom. We didn't have a transmitter, so we'd put some speakers in his front garden, in some bushes, and sort of broadcast it to people who were walking by.
Again, probably over the week, more listeners than this show.

I love the idea, we - it never happened - but I also was hoping that some, maybe some girls would just come by and just, like, sit and listen. "These guys are great. I dunno where these sounds are coming from, it seems to be that bush…

q: Ricky enthused about the neat hole left when a maggot was pulled from a girl's neck on TV. What did Steve conclude?
a: Ricky had watched one show recommended by Karl and turned into Karl
x: Ricky had spent too long with Jonathan Ross
The strong onions had gone to Ricky's head
Ricky had caught a parasite himself
f: "This is it, you watch one program recommended to you by Karl, you've turned into Karl." Steve: "You want a hole in your body?!"
ex: But why would you want to hold in your body like-
No It's got pulling something out, sort of like putting something out your body, It's sort of cleansing, isn't it?
I don't know what you're talking about
No, but it's sort of like, i dont know-
This is it, you watch one program recommended to you by Karl, you've turned into Karl.
You want a hole in your body?!

q: Ricky said that if Karl didn't come back he'd be breaking up the three-way partnership. Steve said Karl was very much like which musician, around 1986-87?
f: Steve predicted Karl would go off and make "quite poor sort of jazz inflected White Man Soul".
ex: Yeah. If Karl doesn't come back, he's breaking up the three way partnership forever.
He's very much like Sting, isn't he?
He's going to go off and sort of make some quite poor sort of jazz inflected White Man Soul and leaving us to go about our business.
Exactly. While I'm going to go into maybe writing some soundtracks.

q: Asked which nation he'd threaten with bombs just to shake them up, who did Steve pick first?
f: Steve: "They've always had it easy, they've always chickened out." Ricky: "It's their equivalent of having Mondays off."
ex: Do you know who I'd threaten?
They've always had it easy, they've always chickened out.
It's their equivalent of having Mondays off.

q: After praising Adam and Joe, who stood in for them on XFM, what cheeky plan did Steve float?
a: Pinching their features, since the show had no ideas
f: Steve: "as we've got no ideas, maybe we could just hijack some of theirs?" Ricky: "Just nick some of theirs."
ex: Well, um, it's interesting, as I was listening to them, they had quite a nice selection of features. They had a couple of good competitions and things. Now, I don't know if, um, having done them for XFM, is it somehow - they may be kind of…
Maybe you could look into that. Obviously not Monday, you’re not here, but —

q: Steve's teenage posing song was the group floor-dance 'Oops Upside Your Head'. How did he describe his performances of it?
a: It was just him, on the floor, in his bedroom
x: His mum kept walking in on him
His brother sat on the record
f: Steve: "One day I thought there'll be other people in this imaginary pose." Ricky pictured "Elbows going everywhere... Knocking over vases."
ex: Mine was, uhhh… mine was Oops Upside Your Head.
It was just me, on the floor, in me bedroom. One day I thought, one day I thought there’ll be other people in this imaginary pose.

q: Ricky explained that the pentatonic scale is basically the black notes on the piano. What did Steve say he could play along with using those?
f: Ricky: "It's the black notes, on the piano." Steve: "Right, that's the one I can play along with Eastenders."
ex: Yeah, no, it is that, it’s that pentatonic scale isn’t it, what is it called?
It’s the black notes, on the piano.
Right, that’s the one I can play along with Eastenders.

q: Hearing that Auntie Nora mashes up leftovers and keeps them in tubs in the fridge, what did Steve first assume?
a: She kept them as a souvenir of each meal she'd had
x: She was saving them to feed the cat
She was saving them for when Karl came round
She was sending them off to be tested
f: Karl corrected him: "No, put it in a pan. Warm it up." Steve: "Oh, that's grotesque."
ex: Put it in the fridge. And she's got in the fridge, it's like January, February, March. She's got all these ice cream boxes that are just full of--
But she doesn't- she reheats it and eats it?
Oh, the- then she, yeah, puts it in the pan.
I thought she was keeping it as a souvenir--
No, put it in a pan. Warm it up.

q: What surprised Steve about Orville the duck?
a: He's still not potty trained, despite mastering speech
x: He's never once taken off his hat
He still hasn't learned to swim
He hasn't aged a day in years
f: "He's been wearing that nappy of his, for years! He can talk, he's mastered the power of speech!"
ex: Just a quick point about Orville - I'm surprised he's still not potty trained.
'Cause he's been, he’s been wearing that nappy of his, for years!
He can talk, he's mastered the power of speech!

q: Comedian Johnny Candon, a big Doctor Who fan, left a comic at Ricky's house. What did Steve do to it?
a: Wrote "GEEK" on post-it notes on every page
x: Coloured in all the Daleks' faces
Filled in the crossword in pen
Swapped the last page for one from the Beano
f: Johnny found them reading it on the tube. Ricky: "That's the sort of vicious man Steve is."
ex: Yeah. In fact, he's - you're right, 'cause um, Johnny bought this comic right, he loves "Doctor Who", and he bought this comic, and Steve, he left it there, and Steve got a post-it note and on every page wrote "GEEK".

Johnny gets it home, reads this, reads it on the tube, and there's "GEEK" written everywhere, on every page. That's the sort of vicious man Steve is. He can hand it out, d'you know’t I mean? Imagine him calling you a geek, what could that-…

q: Steve imagined the circus hippo fuming at being upstaged by the trampolinist. Which of the hippo's own acts did he say was now ruined?
f: Steve's hippo was thinking: "He's already done the trampoline, my pogo stick act is never gonna work!"
ex: This is really annoying. They're going to be... ah no.
He's thinking, he's already done the trampoline, my pogo stick act is never gonna work!

q: Karl's estate neighbours had a lovely baby who grew up playing out till ten and chasing cars. The kid was called Liam. Who did Steve decide it definitely was?
f: Karl's point was the good-looking baby "became an ugly kid" through neglect. Steve's verdict: "It's definitely Liam Gallagher."
ex: Now, the weird thing is it was a good looking kid but as time went on and all that, like, not eating properly and its hair was all
It's not Liam Gallagher is it?
And chasing cars and that and it became an ugly kid.

q: When Ricky said his lizard was about 15 years old, what did Steve presume it gets up to?
a: Listens to a lot of Linkin Park and goes on the internet
x: Sulks in its room and slams doors
Hangs round the bus shelter drinking cider
f: Steve: "Well, I mean it's 15, so presumably it listens to a lot of Linkin Park, goes on the Internet a lot."
ex: About 15 years old right now it.
Knows more now than it did when you got it because it's been in those surroundings, it's had its eye on things.

Well no, what do you think it knows? What do you mean knows more now they act on instinct. What does it learn? It knows when it hears the noise of a plastic case being unwrapped that a crickets gonna fall down any second. That's all it…
Yeah, but it didn't know that in the jungle. So it's already one up. What else has it learned?
Well, I mean it's 15, so presumably it listens to a lot of Linkin park, goes on the Internet a lot.

q: Teenage Steve sat alone for an hour and a half reading philosophy, hoping a girl would think him wise. When she finally walked in, what did she ask?
f: She was soon getting off with Martin Wells, who'd "been dancing around with no trousers on." Steve: "there's a valuable lesson learned."
ex: Um.. Must have sat there for about an hour and a half before anyone came in. And she came in eventually, and I thought, ding dong, this is it. She came in and said, "have you seen Martin Wells?"

I said, "I think you might be next door." She disappeared again. I gave her another 15 minutes on the hope that she'd come back. She didn't... went in the next room, she was getting off with Martin Wells.
Because he'd been dancing. He'd been dancing around with no trousers on.
So all I'll say is there's a valuable lesson learned.

q: Ricky compared Karl to a cat whose owner reckons it can understand what they're saying. What did Steve compare talking to Karl to?
a: Talking to a 14-year-old French exchange student
x: Talking to a parrot that's learned three words
Talking to a satnav with no signal
Talking to a toddler on the phone
f: Steve: "Their English isn't amazing, they roughly understand you, they're trying to piece together what you're saying."
ex: This might be my idea of perfect happiness, being in a room with Karl Pilkington, just watching him, I just watch him look around, when you're talking he looks at you and it's like you know when an owner says it's like the cat can…
It's a bit like having a 14-year-old French exchange student, their English isn't amazing, they roughly understand you, they're trying to piece together what you're saying...

q: As an ironic birthday gift, a friend bought Steve a live video by Ian Moor, Stars in Their Eyes' Chris de Burgh. What was it called?
x: Ian Moor: The Man in Red
f: Steve couldn't work out if it meant "we all know who this guy is" or that he was no longer being Chris de Burgh: "he's just natural."
ex: Well I, it's interesting, my friend bought me, as an ironic gift for my birthday, he bought me the live video of Ian Moor. Um, you'll be pleased to know that 'Lady in Red' was on there...
...among a number of other hits. Em, but it was brilliant, it was called--it had a picture of Ian on the front, it said: "Ian Moor, Naturally"
His jacket was too big for him as well.
Of course. It was ludicrous--but I don't know if that meant "Ian Moor, Naturally", like, we all know who this guy is, it's Ian Moor!
Or was it "Ian Moor", he's no longer being Chris de Burgh, he's just natural.

q: What was Steve's 'very simple test' for whether a band name could ever make it big?
a: Imagine it announced at a huge event: 'Please welcome to the stage...'
x: Ask your nan to say it without laughing
Shout it in a pub and see who turns round
Check it fits on a bus-stop poster
f: Depeche Mode passed the test. According to Steve, "Please welcome to the stage… Ned's Atomic Dustbin!" just doesn't work.
ex: But see, I think this is very, what you just said there is a very good example of why… they are and why certain other bands aren’t, because if you think about it… for me, you see, whenever I think of a band name, if I see a new band’s come…
…or it’s a Nelson Mandela freedom concert…
